references.text: God says to his servant: "I make you a light for the nations." [ref:Isa 49:6|Isaiah 49:6] points forward to the true light that comes into the world to enlighten every person, as described in John 1:9.
[ref:Isa 9:2|Isaiah 9:2] speaks of a people walking in darkness who see a great light. This is a messianic prophecy pointing to Christ as the true light that enlightens every human being.

In [ref:John 8:12|John 8:12], Jesus declares: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life." Here Jesus identifies himself as the true light mentioned in John 1:9.

[ref:John 3:19|John 3:19] states that the light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than the light. This elaborates on the consequences of the true light coming into the world, as described in verse 9.

Jesus says in [ref:John 12:46|John 12:46]: "I have come as a light into the world, so that no one who believes in me should remain in darkness." This is a direct parallel to John 1:9, where the true light comes into the world to enlighten every person.
[ref:1 John 2:8|1 John 2:8] speaks of the true light already shining. John uses the same expression "the true light" (τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινόν) as in John 1:9.

In [ref:Isa 42:6|Isaiah 42:6], God calls his servant to be "a light for the nations." The prophecy of a universal light for all peoples corresponds with the true light enlightening "every person" in John 1:9.

[ref:Ps 36:10|Psalms 36:10]: "For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light." The psalm testifies that God is the source of all light, pointing forward to Christ as the true light in John 1:9.

[ref:John 1:4-5|John 1:4-5] already introduces the theme of light: "In him was life, and the life was the light of people. The light shines in the darkness." Verse 9 elaborates on this by calling it "the true light" that enlightens every person.
In [ref:Acts 26:23|Acts 26:23], Paul says that the Messiah was to "proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles." Christ as light for all people corresponds directly with John 1:9.

[ref:Isa 60:1-2|Isaiah 60:1-2] speaks of the Lord's glory shining forth while darkness covers the earth. The prophecy of God's light breaking through the darkness finds its fulfillment in the true light that comes into the world (John 1:9).
